open_questions: Owner: is the upgrade a late cash sink or an early choice? At 900 it acts as a mid-game sink; at 600 it moves natural decent no-skill win to cycle 23 (below the 26-30 target).
Permit path median drops from 26 (T137) to 24 with upgrades (min 22); still above the cycle-22 early-win check but no longer near the cliff. Retune ship_price or win_cash if the owner wants 26 back.
Gameplay: one upgrade level only (level 2) is modelled; multiple levels are not tuned.
handoff: Route upgrade numbers set: upgrade_cost 600 to 900 (equals ship_price, one price for both choices), upgrade_margin_bonus stays 0.25 (additive on route margin, multiplied with B3 and permit bonus as in sim.margin). data_version 19. sim.py got a --upg flag (with --real): lane cap stays and decent may buy one upgrade per ship. Always-expand never upgrades. Result: decent and always-expand no longer play identically (decent 26 median, always 26 median but decent wins earlier with skills; see details). Always-expand without permit still WINS in real mode (cycle 25, 85 percent): that was already true before T144, the lane cap makes it identical to decent without upgrades, and with upgrades decent beats it by 0-2 cycles only at no-skills. UI/gameplay: sell upgrade only on a full lane.

details.decent_vs_always: With upgrades decent and always-expand differ only slightly at no skills (win cycle 25 both, cash 8952 vs 8892; median 26 both). Upgrade gains show with skills/permit: decent research 23 vs lane-capped baseline 22 to 25 depends on seed. The upgrade does not by itself make always-expand lose; that needs a different fix (for example a saturation or upkeep change), not tuned here.
